caption: Figure 15.3: Protocol for adding and benchmarking a solver arm with wakis.benchmarks.Arm. Subclassing Arm requires three methods—supports(case), resolutions(case), and run(case, h)—which build the mesh for case.cylinders and case.materials, advance the time-domain pulse for case.t_run, sample scattered DFT phasors on concentric case.circles (via circle_points), and return samples, u0, and cost for save_record and cost_to_target.
visual_intent:
Textbook-quality scientific schematic for a computational electromagnetics user manual. Flat vector style on a white background, high contrast, thin dark outlines, generous whitespace, sans-serif labels. Colour code used in every figure: Wakis solver arms and primary field/mesh items in blue, excitation sources and sampling circles in orange, exact analytical references and PEC boundaries in dark grey, dielectric/dispersive materials and target accuracy thresholds in green, unresolved or high-error items in red. Colourblind-safe. Every label must be spelled exactly as listed in this brief; mathematical symbols must be typeset correctly (hats, tildes, subscripts, transposes). Do not add any number, value, equation, software name, product name, logo, watermark or title that is not listed in this brief. Prefer fewer, larger labels over many small ones. No 3D photorealism, no cartoon characters, no hand-drawn or xkcd style.

A left-to-right workflow diagram with a geometric inset. LEFT COLUMN (blue class card 'class MyCustomArm(Arm)'): three method blocks stacked vertically: (1) 'supports(case)' → 'B1-TM, B1-TE, B2-Au-TE', (2) 'resolutions(case)' → 'coarse-to-fine h: [0.10e-6, 0.07e-6, 0.05e-6, 0.035e-6]', (3) 'run(case, h)' expanding rightward into CENTRE PANEL. CENTRE PANEL 'Inside run(case, h)': a 2D circular scatterer ('case.cylinders & case.materials' in green) surrounded by concentric dashed orange sampling rings labelled 'case.circles (circle_points: case.n_points)' and a central origin marker labelled 'incident phasor u0 at origin: shape (n_freq,)', with a time-stepping badge 'run pulse for case.t_run'. RIGHT COLUMN (outputs and aggregation): an arrow exits CENTRE PANEL into a dark grey dictionary box showing the three returned keys: 'samples: (n_freq, len(case.circles), case.n_points)', 'u0: (n_freq,)', and 'cost: {unknowns, steps, dt, run_s, setup_s}'. Below that box, a downward arrow leads to 'save_record(rec, ...)' and finally to a green box 'cost_to_target(records, "q_sca_rms_rel", 0.02)'.

The diagram is structured sequentially in a left-to-right, three-column layout:

**1. Left Column (Solver Arm Definition):**
The column consists of a prominent blue rectangular class card, outlined with a thin dark border, titled with the sans-serif label `class MyCustomArm(Arm)`. Inside this card, three method blocks are stacked vertically:
*   The top block contains the text `supports(case)` pointing to a list: `B1-TM, B1-TE, B2-Au-TE`.
*   The middle block contains the text `resolutions(case)` mapping to the sequence `coarse-to-fine h: [0.10e-6, 0.07e-6, 0.05e-6, 0.035e-6]`.
*   The bottom block displays the method `run(case, h)`.
A distinct directional arrow emerges from the `run(case, h)` block, pointing rightward to visually connect it to the center panel.

**2. Centre Panel (Geometric Inset & Physics Simulation):**
This panel visually represents the simulation space and is headed by the label `Inside run(case, h)`. 
*   In the center is a solid green 2D circular scatterer, visually representing the target material, accompanied by the green label `case.cylinders & case.materials`. 
*   Surrounding this green scatterer are multiple concentric, dashed orange rings. These rings are clearly marked with an orange label reading `case.circles (circle_points: case.n_points)`. 
*   At the exact center of the concentric rings is a distinct origin marker (a small crosshair or dot). An orange line or callout connects this marker to the label `incident phasor u0 at origin: shape (n_freq,)`.
*   Hovering neatly in the corner of this panel is a time-stepping badge or stylized pill shape containing the text `run pulse for case.t_run`, indicating the temporal simulation process.

**3. Right Column (Outputs and Aggregation):**
A dark arrow exits the right side of the Centre Panel and points into the top element of the right column. 
*   This top element is a dark grey rectangular box representing a Python dictionary. Inside the box, the returned output keys and their shapes are listed in crisp sans-serif font:
    *   `samples: (n_freq, len(case.circles), case.n_points)`
    *   `u0: (n_freq,)`
    *   `cost: {unknowns, steps, dt, run_s, setup_s}`
*   From the bottom of this dark grey box, a downward-pointing arrow leads to an intermediate action step simply labeled `save_record(rec, ...)`.
*   Another downward arrow flows from the save record step into the final terminal element: a striking green rectangular box (matching the color code for target accuracy thresholds). This terminal box prominently features the exact text label: `cost_to_target(records, "q_sca_rms_rel", 0.02)`.

All text accurately reflects the specified labels without introducing extraneous numbers, equations, watermarks, or product logos. The spatial arrangement clearly communicates the progression from code architecture (left) to simulated physical geometry (center) and finally to data collection and accuracy evaluation (right).
